# Configuration reference

**Generated, do not edit.** `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` writes this file from the code;
`--check` fails when the two disagree.

- 38 flags in `aries/flags.py`, 23 of them off by default. A flag is read
  with `aries.flags.enabled(name)`. The environment wins over the override file
  (`ARIES_FLAG_FILE`, default `var/flags.env`), and the file wins over the default.
- 187 settings registered with `SettingDef`; the registry was imported (the live registry). A setting
  is changed through the Settings service, the API or the Control Centre, never by editing
  code.

## Flags

Owner = every file outside `aries/flags.py` that names the flag (`git grep -l`).

| flag | default | what it governs | owner |
|---|:-:|---|---|
| `ARIES_CAP_TOPK` | on | the planner is sent the most relevant capabilities, not all of them | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_CLARIFY_RESOLVER` | off | a goal naming one folder gets a code-made, verified listing first; code counts the files whose names fit the request, and only when several fit does one small model call decide, accepted only if it quotes words of the request that fit that file alone, otherwise ARIES asks from a template. Adapted from ClarifyAgent and Ask-before-Plan (aries/workspace/clarify_resolver.py). Off, none of this runs | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py`, `aries/workspace/clarify_resolver.py` |
| `ARIES_COMPLETION_PROGRESS_GUARD` | on | stop after two rejected completion proposals without an intervening action; preserve one correction opportunity | `aries/workspace/agent.py` |
| `ARIES_COMPLETION_READ_PARAPHRASE` | on | the completion contract also recognises read, listing and existence goals said in natural words (exactly one path, nothing else asked) and strips sentence punctuation from paths; done still needs re-checked verified evidence. Off compiles only the anchored sentences, as in ARIES-FINAL-20261006 | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/contracts.py` |
| `ARIES_COMPLETION_TYPED_CONTRACT` | off | when the fast path gives no completion contract, one grammar-constrained call maps an English request to read, list, exists or none with a path and a name; code accepts it only if the path is the one path the request names, verbatim, and the name is empty or verbatim, as an existing contract shape. The model never decides completion (aries/workspace/typed_contract.py, preregistration H5). Off, the module is never imported | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/typed_contract.py` |
| `ARIES_CONTEXT_ENGINE` | on | select memory, recent task history and permitted cached news with provenance, expiry and explicit missing-source coverage | `aries/workspace/agent.py` |
| `ARIES_CONTRACT_FILENAME_JOIN` | off | designed after H5: a read or existence goal that names one folder and one bare file name ("read notes.txt in ~/x") gets a contract for the file in that folder, not for the folder; a read naming a folder and no single file gets no contract, and "show me" a path with an extension is a read, not a listing (aries/workspace/contracts.py). Off, the folder is the target, as in the H5 run | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/contracts.py` |
| `ARIES_CONTRACT_FINISH` | on | propose completion without another model call when every ordered goal condition has verified evidence; fresh independent recheck still required | `aries/workspace/finish_proposal.py` |
| `ARIES_GOAL_TEAMS` | off | decompose eligible goals into scoped temporary read-only runtime agents in the existing queue | `aries/workspace/agent.py` |
| `ARIES_LEARNING_RELATIVE_CTR` | off | designed after MIND: the ordinary learning path judges a topic against this user's pooled engagement rate, each bar the smaller of its setting and 2x (engaged) or 0.5x (ignored) that rate (aries/learning/statistics.py). Off, the absolute settings 0.4 and 0.1 | `aries/learning/loop.py`, `aries/learning/statistics.py` |
| `ARIES_LOOP_GUARD` | off | a planner proposal whose capability and canonical arguments match two earlier steps of the same goal (its second duplicate) ends the goal instead of being rejected and replanned until the step budget is gone; same terminal state as budget exhaustion, stop_reason REPEATED_ACTION, fingerprint and count recorded (aries/workspace/loop_guard.py, docs/AUDIT.md 4b). Off, the loop is unchanged | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/loop_guard.py` |
| `ARIES_MEASURE_CHANGE_HOOK` | off | measurement only (H5 changed_after_read controls): before a finish is re-checked, a goal the runner has armed pauses once so the runner can change a file, then the check proceeds (aries/workspace/measurement_hook.py). Unarmed goals are not affected. Off, the hook module is never imported | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/measurement_hook.py` |
| `ARIES_MEMORY_HYBRID_RRF` | off | designed after LoCoMo: semantic-v3 memory retrieval fuses the cosine ranking with a BM25 ranking of the same rows by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) as its similarity term; recency, importance and layer are added as before (aries/workspace/retrieval.py). Off, cosine only | `aries/workspace/retrieval.py` |
| `ARIES_MEMORY_SIMILARITY_RANK` | off | designed after M1 (LoCoMo): semantic-v3 memory retrieval orders by the similarity term alone (with ARIES_MEMORY_HYBRID_RRF, the fused rank); recency, importance and layer only break ties (aries/workspace/retrieval.py). Off, the weighted sum | `aries/workspace/retrieval.py` |
| `ARIES_MK_FROZEN` | on | Macedonian is frozen: it keeps working and keeps being tested, and nothing new is built on it | `aries/workspace/clarify_resolver.py` |
| `ARIES_NEWS_DIVERSE_TOPK` | off | designed after MIND: the briefing picks by Maximal Marginal Relevance (lambda 0.7, topic redundancy) instead of round-robin over topics (aries/news/selection.py). Off, round-robin | `aries/news/selection.py` |
| `ARIES_PLANNER_CLARIFY` | on | the planner may stop and ask which target is meant when its own verified observations show several that fit the goal; every choice must name something observed. Off removes the option from the grammar and the prompt | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_PLANNER_CLARIFY_GUARD` | off | with ARIES_PLANNER_CLARIFY: a question carries no capability or arguments (grammar), confirming is ask_approval and asking is only for choosing between observed targets (prompt), and a named but unlisted folder is listed before anything is read in it. Off leaves the clarification grammar and prompt unchanged | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_PLANNER_GATE_HINT` | off | with ARIES_ROUTER_CAPABILITY_GATE: the planner is told which capability the gate chose as the first step. Off, the planner does not see it | `aries/intelligence/capability_gate.py`, `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_PLANNER_OOS_ACTION` | off | designed after R1: when fail is allowed, the planner is told to choose fail with reason OUT_OF_SCOPE when no capability fulfils the goal completely, instead of the nearest capability. Off, no such message | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_PLANNER_PER_CAP_GRAMMAR` | off | designed after R1: the planner grammar has one branch per capability with that capability's own required arguments, so an action missing a required argument cannot be generated (aries/workspace/agent_planner.py). Off, the flat grammar | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_PLAN_DISPATCH_FIX` | off | when the planner context's own audit metadata (one omitted_items entry per memory dropped for budget, source_status, preferences) exceeds the 2,500-character budget, it is compacted (counts instead of entries, then source_status dropped, then preferences shortened) instead of failing the goal before its first planner call with 'Context metadata exceeds planner budget' (docs/AUDIT.md 7.2: the six never-planned held-out goals). Off, the error is raised as frozen | `aries/workspace/context_engine.py` |
| `ARIES_PLAN_MEMORY` | on | relevant remembered facts are injected into planning | `aries/workspace/agent.py` |
| `ARIES_READ_PATH_STRICT` | off | the legacy read_file route takes only the path token: it starts at the first / or ~/, filler words before it are allowed and any other words send the goal to the planner, it ends at the longest existing name or the first component with an extension, and a sentence-final mark is stripped only when the name without it exists or has an extension (docs/AUDIT.md 4a). Off, the capture is the rest of the sentence, as frozen | `aries/workspace/capabilities.py` |
| `ARIES_RESOLVER_CODE_SELECT` | off | designed after H4b, with ARIES_CLARIFY_RESOLVER: no model call decides between candidates; code selects the one candidate a request word or order word singles out (the same check that guarded the model's span), otherwise ARIES asks (aries/workspace/clarify_resolver.py). Off, the decision call runs, as in the H4b run | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/clarify_resolver.py` |
| `ARIES_ROUTER_ABSTAIN` | on | the router may answer ASK or OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than choosing the nearest action; off restores the pre-2026-10-03 instruction to pick the nearest one regardless | `aries/intelligence/router.py` |
| `ARIES_ROUTER_CAPABILITY_GATE` | off | designed after R1: when a local router decision would act, one grammar-constrained call names the registered capability that fulfils the request completely, or OUT_OF_SCOPE, which turns the decision into OUT_OF_SCOPE; it never turns an abstention into an action (aries/intelligence/capability_gate.py). Off, the module is never imported | `aries/intelligence/capability_gate.py`, `aries/intelligence/router.py`, `aries/intelligence/schemas.py`, `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_ROUTER_SURFACE_CONSISTENT` | off | designed after R1: the router's abstention text no longer says the listed capabilities are never OUT_OF_SCOPE, says a request needing something none of them does is OUT_OF_SCOPE, and names email and calendar as having no capability. Off, the frozen A1 text | `aries/intelligence/router.py` |
| `ARIES_STATE_SNAPSHOT` | on | the planner is given the current desktop state before it plans | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_TERMINAL_READ_FAILURE` | on | stop repeated model planning after an actual nonretryable missing-file error for the exact single requested read | `aries/workspace/terminal_failure.py` |
| `ARIES_TILE_HIDPI` | on | desktop.tile reads the monitor's scale factor from Mutter and expects the device-pixel-aligned rectangle, so a correct tile on a fractionally scaled display is not reported unverified | `aries/workspace/desktop_capabilities.py` |
| `ARIES_TRACE_FEWSHOT` | on | similar past successful plans are offered to the planner | `aries/workspace/agent.py`, `aries/workspace/traces.py` |
| `ARIES_TYPED_CONTRACT_CODE_PATH` | off | designed after H5, with ARIES_COMPLETION_TYPED_CONTRACT: the model returns only the goal type and a verbatim name, and code supplies the one path the request names; a read of a folder with no name is rejected (aries/workspace/typed_contract.py). Off, the model copies the path, as in the H5 run | `aries/workspace/typed_contract.py` |
| `ARIES_TYPE_STRICT` | on | input.type_text refuses any case that would silently lose characters — a NUL, a filtered control character, a line break into a single-line control, a rejected or partially landed write — instead of returning a success carrying landed=false | `aries/workspace/input_capabilities.py` |
| `ARIES_VERIFY_FEEDBACK` | on | the planner is told whether each past step's effect was INDEPENDENTLY OBSERVED, not merely whether the tool returned. Off leaves the loop, the retry policy and the step history untouched and removes only that — the one variable in the state-verification-feedback experiment | `aries/workspace/agent_planner.py` |
| `ARIES_VERIFY_HARDENED` | off | the 23 verifiers the frozen review classed TRIVIAL, SELF_REPORT or PLANNER_SUPPLIED also require the report to agree with a fresh read (a different channel where one exists, measured drift for volatile values), per-capability invariants, and UNVERIFIED when that read fails (aries/workspace/hardened_verifiers.py, preregistration H8). Read when the registry is imported. Off, every verifier is the frozen function | `aries/workspace/hardened_verifiers.py`, `aries/workspace/registry.py` |
| `ARIES_VERIFY_HARDENED_EXTRA` | off | exploratory, designed after H8 baseline-2: the same hardening for two INDEPENDENT verifiers, notification.send and system.disk. Not part of the confirmatory H8 test | `aries/workspace/hardened_verifiers.py`, `aries/workspace/registry.py` |
| `ARIES_VERIFY_SCOPE` | off | exploratory, designed after H8: the 14 capabilities of the H8 side_effect_outside_scope operator snapshot their declared scope before the executor runs (parent folder of each path, the other windows, the notification table) and their verifier fails when anything in it other than the target changed; an unreadable scope is UNVERIFIED (aries/workspace/scope_verifiers.py, docs/AUDIT.md 4e). Read when the registry is imported. Off, every verifier is the frozen function | `aries/workspace/registry.py`, `aries/workspace/scope_verifiers.py` |

## Settings

Module = the file and line of the `SettingDef` call.

| key | type | default | section | title — description | module |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai.context_tokens` | int | `8192` | ai | **Context window** — How much conversation and document text the local model may hold at once. Larger remembers more but costs video memory and reloads the model; the local runtime, not ARIES, decides what it can fit. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:87` |
| `ai.daily_cost_limit` | float | `0.0` | ai | **Daily cost limit** — Maximum spend on paid model calls per day. 0 means no limit is enforced. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:59` |
| `ai.max_output_tokens` | int | `4096` | ai | **Maximum answer length** — Longest answer the local model may produce in one turn. Lower it for terse replies and faster responses; a task that needs more than it gets fails loudly rather than returning a truncated answer. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:95` |
| `ai.prefer_local` | bool | `false` | ai | **Prefer local models** — Route work to a locally hosted model whenever one can do the job, for privacy. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:53` |
| `ai.provider_priority` | list | `["cli", "ollama", "openai"]` | ai | **Model priority** — Order in which model providers are tried; the first reachable one is used. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:50` |
| `ai.reasoning_depth` | str | `balanced` | ai | **Reasoning depth** — How much deliberation to spend per task where the provider supports it. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:56` |
| `ai.send_file_contents` | bool | `false` | ai | **Allow file contents to leave the machine** — Whether a cloud model may receive the contents of local files, rather than only their names. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:62` |
| `ai.temperature` | float | `0.1` | ai | **Temperature** — How much the model gambles on less likely words. 0 is repeatable and literal; around 0.7 is conversational; above 1.2 it invents. Structured extraction and routing decisions are more reliable low. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:71` |
| `ai.top_p` | float | `0.9` | ai | **Top-p (nucleus)** — Keeps only the most likely words whose probabilities add up to this fraction. 1.0 considers everything; 0.5 keeps the model on the obvious path. Temperature is the dial to try first — this one mostly matters above temperature 1. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:79` |
| `automations.breaker_cooldown_minutes` | int | `30` | automations | **Wait before retrying** — How long ARIES waits after pausing a failing automation before allowing one trial run. | `aries/automations/breaker.py:61` |
| `automations.breaker_threshold` | int | `3` | automations | **Failures before pausing** — How many unsuccessful passes in a row (failed or degraded unless the workflow explicitly exempts partial diagnostic passes) before ARIES stops running it and waits. Set to 0 to never pause a failing automation. | `aries/automations/breaker.py:56` |
| `automations.check_interval_seconds` | int | `60` | automations | **Dispatcher cadence** — How often ARIES asks which automations are due. This is not how often they run — each automation has its own interval. | `aries/automations/worker.py:50` |
| `automations.worker_enabled` | bool | `false` | automations | **Run automations in the background** — Whether ARIES runs enabled automations on their own schedule. Off means automations only run when explicitly asked. | `aries/automations/worker.py:46` |
| `autonomy.level` | str | `manual` | autonomy | **Autonomy level** — How much ARIES may do without asking. manual: agents only suggest. assisted: low-risk actions run automatically. automated: approved workflow categories run on their own. custom: permissions set individually. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:36` |
| `autonomy.max_actions_per_hour` | int | `30` | autonomy | **Action budget** — Maximum side-effecting actions ARIES may take in one hour before it must stop and ask. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:45` |
| `autonomy.require_approval_risk` | str | `medium` | autonomy | **Always ask above risk** — Lowest risk tier that always requires a human approval before execution. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:42` |
| `brief.window_hours` | float | `24.0` | briefing | **Look back over** — How far back a brief reaches for news and changes. Should normally match how often the brief is produced. | `aries/brief/settings.py:7` |
| `briefing.length` | str | `standard` | briefing | **Briefing length** — How much detail a briefing carries. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:131` |
| `briefing.morning_enabled` | bool | `false` | briefing | **Morning brief** — Whether the Morning Intelligence Brief is produced. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:127` |
| `briefing.morning_time` | str | `07:30` | briefing | **Morning brief time** — Local time the morning brief is delivered, as HH:MM. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:129` |
| `briefing.sections` | list | `["decisions", "system", "news", "automations", "learning"]` | briefing | **Briefing sections** — Which sections the brief contains, in order. Available: decisions, system, news, automations, learning, calendar, email, projects. | `aries/settings/defaults.py:139` |
| `connect.attention_enabled` | bool | `false` | connect | **Attention Pass** — Read the sources you have connected, understand each item on the local model, and tell you what needs you. Reports only — it never replies, forwards, deletes or marks anything as read. | `aries/connect/automation.py:51` |
| `connect.attention_interval_minutes` | int | `60` | connect | **How often to look** — How often the Attention Pass reads your connected sources. | `aries/connect/automation.py:57` |
| `connect.enabled` | bool | `false` | connect | **Let ARIES read connected sources** — Whether ARIES may read the folders and mailboxes you have connected. Off means a source can be registered and checked, and nothing is read. | `aries/connect/settings.py:14` |
| `connect.mail_days` | int | `3` | connect | **How far back to read mail** — Messages older than this are not fetched on a routine read. ARIES is answering 'what needs me now', not archiving your mailbox. | `aries/connect/settings.py:31` |
| `connect.max_items_per_read` | int | `40` | connect | **How much to take at once** — A cap on items per read, so one enormous folder or a busy inbox cannot become one enormous working set. | `aries/connect/settings.py:26` |
| `connect.report_injection_attempts` | bool | `true` | connect | **Tell me when content tries to give ARIES orders** — Content that contains instructions aimed at the assistant is reported next to its summary. | `connect.understand_locally` | bool | `true` | connect | **Understand content only on this machine** — Summarising and classifying what ARIES read happens on the local model and nowhere else. Turning this off would allow the contents of your files and mail to be sent to whichever model provider is configured. | `aries/connect/settings.py:19` |
| `data.clean_interval_hours` | int | `24` | data | **How often to check** — How often ARIES looks for data past its window. | `aries/lifecycle/settings.py:27` |
| `data.cleaning_enabled` | bool | `false` | data | **Delete old data automatically** — Whether ARIES removes data that has passed its retention window. Off means nothing is ever deleted — the database grows without limit, and `aries data clean` is the only way anything goes. | `aries/lifecycle/settings.py:15` |
| `data.dry_run_first` | bool | `true` | data | **Show before deleting** — Record what a cleaning pass WOULD remove, and act only on the next pass if nothing changed. The first run of anything that deletes should be a rehearsal. | `aries/lifecycle/settings.py:21` |
| `data.enabled` | bool | `false` | data | **Data lifecycle** — Whether ARIES removes data that has passed its retention window, on a schedule. Off means nothing is ever deleted automatically. | `aries/lifecycle/automation.py:20` |
| `data.keep_automation_logs_days` | int | `14` | data | **Automation logs** — Line-by-line output of automation runs. Worth having while diagnosing something that just went wrong; worthless a fortnight later, and by far the fastest-growing table in the database.  Minimum 2 days, because the Automations screen's last-run detail read it. | `aries/lifecycle/settings.py:39 (key computed)` |
| `data.keep_automation_runs_days` | int | `90` | data | **Automation runs** — One row per run. | `data.keep_health_samples_days` | int | `90` | data | **Health samples** — Individual probe readings. | `data.keep_news_days` | int | `45` | data | **News items** — Articles ARIES collected, with what it delivered and held. | `data.keep_notifications_days` | int | `60` | data | **Notifications** — Delivery decisions, including the ones held back. Kept long enough to answer 'why did you not tell me about this?'. | `data.keep_resource_events_days` | int | `90` | data | **Resource events** — When the resource policy refused heavy work or let go again. | `data.keep_task_history_days` | int | `90` | data | **Tasks** — The engine's task records. Kept as long as the runs that reference them.  Minimum 14 days, because task traces in the Control Centre read it. | `aries/lifecycle/settings.py:39 (key computed)` |

| `learning.damping` | float | `0.5` | learning | **Damping per reversal** — How much smaller each change becomes after ARIES turns around on the same target. 0.5 halves the allowed step per reversal, so an oscillation decays instead of continuing at full amplitude. | `aries/learning/settings.py:50` |

| `learning.fatigue_step` | float | `0.05` | learning | **Fading interest step** — How much a weight decays per pass when interest is declining steadily rather than contradicted outright. | `aries/learning/settings.py:76` |

| `learning.max_reversals` | int | `3` | learning | **Give up after changing my mind** — How many times ARIES may reverse a previous adjustment to the same thing before it stops adjusting it and leaves the decision to the user. 0 disables freezing, and the damping alone slows an oscillation. | `aries/learning/settings.py:45` |
| `learning.max_step` | float | `0.15` | learning | **Largest single change** — How far one learning pass may move any weight. A bug in the evidence should cost a nudge, not a configuration. | `aries/learning/settings.py:40` |

| `learning.noisy_threshold` | float | `0.3` | learning | **Too much noise above** — Share of delivered items dismissed before ARIES offers to raise the relevance bar. It only ever offers to be quieter, never louder. | `aries/learning/settings.py:36` |
| `learning.reversal_confirmations` | int | `2` | learning | **Passes before reversing** — How many consecutive learning passes must reach the same conclusion before a reversal is applied. This is what separates a change of mind from a bad fortnight. | `aries/learning/settings.py:67` |
| `learning.reversal_hysteresis` | float | `0.4` | learning | **Harder to reverse than to keep** — How much stricter the evidence must be to REVERSE an established preference than to continue it, from 0 to 1. 0 makes reversing as easy as forming a preference, which is how learned values start oscillating. | `aries/learning/settings.py:57` |

| `news.local_summaries` | bool | `false` | news | **Macedonian local summaries** — Summarize selected briefing items locally; cache results and retain originals on failure. | `aries/news/settings.py:36` |
| `news.max_age_hours` | float | `72.0` | news | **Ignore items older than** — Entries published longer ago than this are not treated as news. | `aries/news/settings.py:12` |
| `news.max_bytes_per_source` | int | `4000000` | news | **Maximum download** — Largest response ARIES will read from one source. Anything beyond this is truncated rather than buffered. | `aries/news/settings.py:18` |

| `power.allow_gpu_jobs` | bool | `false` | power | **Allow heavy GPU jobs while the display is off** — Sustained GPU work — local model inference or training — is refused while the display is off unless this is on.
